citation: Farber, Hahn, Hell & Miller, Concerning the achromatic number of graphs, JCTB 40 (1986) 21-39 (FPT); Kolay, Panolan, Saurabh et al., Parameterized Reunion with Achromatic Number, ISAAC 2025
note: FPT parameterized by k (2^{O(k^5)}+O(|E|)). A polynomial kernel is known only on restricted classes (d-degenerate graphs, trees); for general graphs the poly-kernel question is explicitly stated open in ISAAC 2025. No coNP-based lower bound known.

citation: Basavaraju, Panolan, Rai, Ramanujan & Saurabh, On the Kernelization Complexity of String Problems, Theoretical Computer Science 730 (2018) 21-31
note: FPT by d (Gramm-Niedermeier-Rossmanith d^d). No polynomial kernel unless NP⊆coNP/poly, for the distance parameter d and any fixed alphabet of size >=2, via cross-composition. FPT algorithm exists but is incompressible.

citation: Fomin, Le, Lokshtanov, Saurabh, Thomassé & Zehavi, Subquadratic Kernels for Implicit 3-Hitting Set and 3-Set Packing Problems, ACM Trans. Algorithms 15(1) (2019) [SODA 2018]; earlier: Gramm, Guo, Hüffner & Niedermeier, Theory Comput. Syst. 38 (2005)
note: Deletion to a disjoint union of cliques = hitting all induced P3's (implicit 3-Hitting Set). Poly kernel; state of the art O(k^{5/3}) vertices.

citation: Guo & Uhlmann, Kernelization and Complexity Results for Connectivity Augmentation Problems, Networks 56(2) (2010) 131-142 [WADS 2007]
note: For augmenting to bridge-connectivity (2-edge-connected) and to biconnectivity (2-vertex-connected) by adding k links: problem kernel with O(k^2) vertices and links. Poly kernel.

citation: Bodlaender, Thomassé & Yeo, Kernel bounds for disjoint cycles and disjoint paths, Theoretical Computer Science 412(35) (2011) 4570-4578 [ESA 2009]
note: FPT by k (Erdős-Pósa). Disjoint Cycles has no polynomial kernel unless NP⊆coNP/poly, via composition + transformation from Disjoint Factors.

citation: Xiao & Kou, Kernelization and Parameterized Algorithms for 3-Path Vertex Cover, TAMC 2017, LNCS 10185, 654-668; general bound: Abu-Khzam, A kernelization algorithm for d-Hitting Set, JCSS 76 (2010)
note: 3-PVC = hit every P3 (a 3-element set) = 3-Hitting Set, so O(k^2) kernel follows; Xiao-Kou give a dedicated 5k-vertex (linear) kernel. Poly kernel.

citation: Bazgan, Chopin & Fellows, Parameterized Complexity of the Firefighter Problem, ISAAC 2011, LNCS 7074, 643-652; Bazgan, Chopin, Cygan, Fellows, Fomin & van Leeuwen, JCSS 80 (2014) 1285-1297
note: OFF-SCHEMA: this parameterization is W[1]-hard, even on bipartite graphs (Saving-k-Vertices). Not FPT unless FPT=W[1], hence NO kernel of any size exists -- kernelization presupposes FPT. The row's parameterized=FPT is inconsistent with its own canonical_task_param text. Flagged; does not fit the four-way FPT-kernel dichotomy.

citation: Mahajan & Raman, Parameterizing above guaranteed values: MaxSat and MaxCut, Journal of Algorithms 31(2) (1999) 335-354
note: Any CNF with m clauses has an assignment satisfying >= m/2, so k<=m/2 is trivially yes; a nontrivial instance has m<2k clauses, and each 2-clause has <=2 vars => <=4k vars. Linear kernel.

parameterization: excess above the tight (7/8)m guarantee, k
citation: Alon, Gutin, Kim, Szeider & Yeo, Solving MAX-r-SAT above a tight lower bound, Algorithmica 61(3) (2011) 638-655 [SODA 2010]
note: Satisfy >= (7/8)m + k clauses. FPT with a kernel of O(k^2) variables (fixed r=3) via the Fourier/algebraic above-average technique; poly(k) total size. Poly kernel.

citation: Bordewich & Semple, On the computational complexity of the rooted subtree prune and regraft distance, Annals of Combinatorics 8 (2005) 409-423
note: Rooted MAF is FPT by k; the subtree and chain reduction rules yield a linear kernel (O(k) leaves). Poly (linear) kernel.

citation: Zehavi, Maximum Minimal Vertex Cover Parameterized by Vertex Cover, SIAM J. Discrete Math. 31(4) (2017) 2440-2456 [MFCS 2015]
note: FPT parameterized by vc(G). No polynomial kernel unless NP⊆coNP/poly, even on bipartite graphs (cross-composition).

citation: Gutin, Muciaccia & Yeo, (Non-)existence of polynomial kernels for the Test Cover problem, Information Processing Letters 113(4) (2013) 123-126
note: FPT by k. Parameterization 'a test cover with at most k tests' has no polynomial kernel unless coNP⊆NP/poly (cross-composition + parametric duality). A poly kernel exists only if test sizes are bounded by a constant.

citation: Cygan, Kratsch, Pilipczuk, Pilipczuk & Wahlström, Clique Cover and Graph Separation: New Incompressibility Results, ACM Trans. Comput. Theory 6(2) (2014) [ICALP 2012]
note: FPT by k (Marx-Razgon; Bousquet-Daligault-Thomassé). Edge/Vertex Multicut parameterized by cutset size has no polynomial kernel unless NP⊆coNP/poly.

citation: Kratsch & Wahlström, Representative sets and irrelevant vertices, FOCS 2012 (poly kernel for BOUNDED #terminals, O(k^{s+1})); Wahlström, Quasipolynomial Multicut-mimicking Networks..., ACM Trans. Algorithms 18(3) (2022) [ICALP 2020]
note: FPT by s. A (randomized) polynomial kernel is known only when the number of terminals is a constant; for unbounded terminals only a quasipolynomial kernel is known. Existence of a polynomial kernel for the general (undirected) problem is open; the coNP lower bound of Cygan et al. covers only the DIRECTED variant.

citation: Jansen, Lokshtanov & Saurabh, A near-optimal planarization algorithm, SODA 2014, 1802-1811 (FPT); Jansen & Włodarczyk, Lossy Planarization, STOC 2022 (approximate kernel)
note: FPT (2^{O(k log k)} n). Vertex Planarization is NOT a Planar-F-Deletion instance (F={K5,K3,3} contains no planar graph), so the FLMS kernelization does not apply. Existence of a (true) polynomial kernel is a well-known open problem; only a constant-factor lossy/approximate kernel is known. No coNP lower bound established.

citation: Hanan (1966) + Dreyfus & Wagner (1971) (FPT via Hanan grid DP); cf. Dom, Lokshtanov & Saurabh, Incompressibility through Colors and IDs, ICALP 2009 (graph Steiner Tree by #terminals: no poly kernel unless coNP⊆NP/poly)
note: FPT by k. No polynomial kernel is known. The general graph Steiner Tree lower bound (Dom-Lokshtanov-Saurabh) does not transfer to the geometric rectilinear special case, and the Hanan grid yields a poly(k)-size PLANAR-GRAPH instance rather than a rectilinear kernel (and does not bound coordinate magnitudes). Neither a poly kernel nor a lower bound is established for the geometric version.

citation: Lokshtanov & Sloper, Fixed Parameter Set Splitting, Linear Kernel and Improved Running Time, ACiD 2005 (Algorithms and Complexity in Durham), 105-113
note: Max Set Splitting: a random 2-colouring splits >= half the sets, so k<=m/2 is trivially yes; combined with reduction rules this gives a linear (O(k)) kernel. Poly kernel.

citation: Sánchez-Arroyo, Determining the total colouring number is NP-hard, Discrete Math. 78 (1989) 315-319 (NP-hardness); Bodlaender, Jansen & Kratsch, Cross-composition, SIAM J. Discrete Math. 28(1) (2014) [STACS 2011]; Drucker, New limits to classical and quantum instance compression, SIAM J. Comput. 44(5) (2015) [FOCS 2012] (AND-composition)
note: FPT by treewidth (Courcelle/MSO). No polynomial kernel unless coNP⊆NP/poly, by AND-cross-composition: for a disjoint union tw = max_i tw(G_i) <= max input size, and χ''(union)=max_i χ''(G_i), so 'chi'' <= r' composes as AND from NP-hard Total Coloring. (Standard disjoint-union argument, same mechanism as q-Coloring-by-treewidth; derived, not a single named theorem for total coloring.)

citation: Fellows, Heggernes, Rosamond, Sloper & Telle, Finding k Disjoint Triangles in an Arbitrary Graph, WG 2004, LNCS 3353, 235-244; subquadratic: Fomin et al., ACM Trans. Algorithms 15(1) (2019)
note: Vertex-disjoint Triangle Packing = 3-Set Packing on the triangle hypergraph; crown-decomposition/3-Set-Packing kernelization gives O(k^2) vertices (subquadratic in later work). Poly kernel.
